timing.label: Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: How do I know an agent didn't skip endpoints and call it clean?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: Why pay for a fan-out of agents when one engineer could read 22 endpoints in an afternoon?

problem.quote: You get a verdict for every endpoint the API serves

approach.quote: one audit agent per route file, a fixer per file with a confirmed leak, and a separate verifier

evidence.quote: A separate verifier agent wrote its own check and returned pass

next_step.quote: Ask: approve the full run at a ten ACU cap

must_mention.point: Every endpoint covered: the count comes from the code (22 in 7 route files) and a small slice ran first
must_mention.evidence_quote: twenty-two endpoints in seven route files, and the count comes from the code

must_mention.point: The confirmed leak: the single-order read filters on id alone, so staff of one brand can read the other brand's order
must_mention.evidence_quote: The single-order read filters on the order id alone, so a merchandiser or admin of one brand can read the other brand's order

must_mention.point: A failed or invalid agent was caught in code with a bounded retry, and resuming the same run ID replayed finished agents
must_mention.evidence_quote: The script caught the error and retried each one once

must_mention.point: The fix lives on a throwaway branch named by the script, a separate agent verified it, and main keeps the defect
must_mention.evidence_quote: on a throwaway branch named by the script, with the planted test un-skipped. A separate verifier agent wrote its own check

must_mention.point: Cost quoted per agent from the run (roughly 0.7–1.0 ACU each, about 3.5 for the slice) with a projection for the full run
must_mention.evidence_quote: zero point nine nine ACU to audit carts, zero point seven one for orders, zero point nine six for the fix and zero point eight four for the verifier

article_plural_slips: "each one has a file and line" — "a file-and-line reference" reads cleaner
sentences_to_rerecord: Cost: three and a half ACU for the slice.

accuracy.anchor: All five points with quotable sentences and per-agent numbers (anchors: 27–30 every point with a number; 15–20 three of five; under 10 one point).

structure.anchor: Verdict → coverage → failure → fix → cost → ask held, including after the interruption (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only).

customer_relevance.anchor: Used the auditor's own terms: endpoint count, independent verifier, per-agent cost, freeze on main (anchors: 16–20 auditor's numbers and constraints used; 10–13 some numbers; under 6 feature talk).

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: All six segments within ±5 s; one filler in about 8 minutes (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off).

recovery.anchor: Both objections ran acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer; the commercial one used four per-agent ACU figures (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern).

stems: "The number first: …" — lead every answer to "how many" with the figure.
"The settled figure is…" — say which ACU number you quote and why, before you are asked.
"No agent decides the list; the script does." — keep the boundary to one sentence.
previous_run_comparison: Second grading of the same transcript; scores within 1 point of run 1.
